Bobrovytsya Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Chernihiv Oblast, Ukraine

Demolished. Bobrovytsya's earliest known Jewish community formed in the first half of the 19th century, opening a prayer house in 1869; by 1889, Abraham Getselev Tseitlin served as rabbi, with Mezhirov Berko Mihelev as gabay and Eliyash Epshtein as treasurer. The population reached 671 by 1897. The town suffered three pogroms: on October 27, 1905, 27 Jewish shops were robbed; on September 2, 1919, four Jews were killed by units of Denikin's Army; and on January 2, 1920, the Romashko gang killed 38 Jews. By 1926, only 154 Jews remained; an estimated 17 were killed following the September 1941 German occupation. This cemetery, said to have been established in the 19th century, saw its last known Hasidic burial in 1941, and was demolished in the late 1980s.
